title: COVETOUS EYES WILL BE PUT OUT

sense.text:
“Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh.” Walking in the spirit means walking in the ordinances, the laws, the statutes and the commandments of the Lord God. If you are doing these things, you are never going to do amiss.

This is where covetousness starts and where it is stopped. A covetous man is giving in to his lust. The blueprint is in the Bible: it tells you exactly what to do to have life, but every day you get up you choose the things that bring death to your door. When a man among us lets his lust control him, that shows he is not studying and not reading. That is how we judge, according to the scriptures: we sift a man through the Bible and believe what the Bible says he is, not what he says about himself.

We are supposed to be our brother's keeper, and the way to be a brother's keeper is by dealing right in everything we choose to do. Don't push people to the edge: everybody comes from different walks of life, and with bad dealings you could be the reason a brother doesn't get the kingdom, making him revert back to the man he used to be.

The solution to every sin a man finds in himself is this first verse. Walk in the spirit. Start reading the Bible, start applying what you read, and that spirit is not going to destroy you.

“For the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh.” There is a war within you. The old man always wants to be around, always in your business: you don't need to read the Bible, let's go rob a house, let's go steal a car, remember how you used to boost cars, you're broke, call your man. The only way to win that war is to actually read your Bible and apply what you read.

“And these are contrary the one to the other: so that ye cannot do the things that ye would.” The flesh is always going to be present. What you put in you now is what fights the flesh. If the spirit is in you, you subdue your own understanding and all the evil that is in you every time it pops its head up.

The Bible should be like the receptionist at the front desk of an office building: nobody gets in to see anyone unless she lets them in. The door to your soul is your forehead, and the Bible should sit there. Then you are like the old head on the block: I hear you, that's a good plan, but that's two to five; that's ten to fifteen; that's life, don't do it. When you see a beautiful woman, you remember Job's covenant with his eyes. When a stack of money is sitting there and nobody is around, thou shalt not steal. Without the scriptures readily in your mind, it is impossible not to fall into temptation.

The man who never reads, never prays, never fasts, misses the new moons and the feast days and shows up on the Sabbath only to keep up appearances is not walking in the spirit, and he cannot fight the lust in his flesh. Most High will reveal him: we are not small anymore, people watch us, and a brother doing wickedness in fringes gets found out, even states away.

precepts.why:
“For we know that the law is spiritual: but I am carnal, sold under sin.” This is the spirit you must be in so that you do not do amiss: the law is spiritual. We are carnal, sold under sin.

So if we want to stop being carnal, if we want to stop sinning, we have to keep the law. Walking in the spirit is keeping the law.

“It is the spirit that quickeneth”: only the spirit can change you as a man. “The flesh profiteth nothing.”

“The words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life.” The words of the Lord are the spirit. So when Galatians says walk in the spirit, it means walk in the ordinances, the laws, the statutes and the commandments of the Lord God. Do these things and you are never going to do amiss.

“Blessed is he that readeth.” Everybody wants blessings, and here is the formula for them. The bishop always says read four chapters a day and you finish the Bible in a year, and if you have more time, read a lot more.

The blessing comes this way: “and they that hear the words of this prophecy, and keep those things which are written therein.” If you read, you hear the word and apply it in your life. You read that thou shalt not steal, you apply it, and you don't have to worry about anybody calling you a thief.

Plenty of people say they read a good book a week. There are plenty of books, but you should be reading this book, because this is the book of life.

“This is the book of the commandments of God”: when you want to know what commandments to follow, you have to read the whole Bible. “And the law that endureth for ever.” Forever.

All the Christian churches are lost in the sauce, saying you don't have to keep any laws. The simple way to prove they are all greedy dogs and covetous men: as much as they say the laws are done away, they keep the one law that actually is done away with, tithing. That means they are covetous, and all their lights are going to get put out. So coming out of the Christian church and seeing that covetousness is a bad thing, why would we be in the truth and still be covetous? It makes no damn sense.

“All they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.” If you want life, if you don't want your light put out, you have to keep the commandments. That is how you end up blessed: you read the Bible, learn all the laws, statutes and commandments, and apply them. The fact that you are here means you want life; but are you going to do what is necessary for eternal life, or revert back to the old man and start giving in to your lust again?

“Whatsoever thou takest in hand, remember the end, and thou shalt never do amiss.” You have to have a disciplined heart and think before you act, because naturally the flesh wants evil in every situation. Remember the ultimate end, which is fire.

Remember the end of every action. If I steal, I might get caught and end up in jail, or somebody might punch me out, and some dudes will shoot you. In the street dudes would shoot a man for a dollar, and it was never about the money, it was about the principle. So even in the world there are principles. How can you be in the truth with no principles, doing it with fringes on, making people speak evil of the gospel?

So if you are in business, don't shortchange people and don't steal their money. Think of the worst a man could do to you, and if that doesn't scare you, forget men and think of what the Most High can do to you for defrauding your brothers and being covetous. Every one of us has to take inventory, acknowledge our sins and recognize the demons that plague us, because the demons are never gone: they wait right outside the door, like the vampire that turns into a bat at sunrise and comes right back out when the sun goes down. When people keep bringing up your hidden sins, that is the Most High putting your business out there to give you a chance to change, before he puts your light out.

sense.text: “But godliness with contentment is great gain.” That little verse will save your life. Be content with the things the Lord gives you.

“For we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out.” You come in naked, and the only thing you get when you leave, depending on where and how you die, is a coffin and a garment. You are taking nothing with you, so why would you mess up your eternal life for money, cars and houses, vain things that do not profit?

“And having food and raiment let us be therewith content.” The covetous man says, I've got food and clothes, but I need money for all the new clothes; I'm not happy with the little I have; I want everything right now at any expense.

“But they that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare, and into many foolish and hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition.” If all you want to do is get paid, you are going to die. Like 50 said, get rich or die trying: you're going to die.

“For the love of money is the root of all evil.” If you love money too much you will do anything for it. If you rob and steal and lie to get paid, you will kill for it too. And when you defraud your brother, that is hatred. Brothers among us are broke, trying to make a living; if you love your brothers, why would you defraud a brother who is broke just like you? And don't go cozying up under the few brothers who have money because they have money.

“Which while some coveted after”: you are covetous when you see the things you want and can't get them, and you find every other means to get them. Some of you need to work for somebody and leave business alone, because business has to be done righteously, and a covetous man's business never prospers, or prospers only in unrighteousness until he does it to the wrong person. Remember the two wicked elders out of Babylon who thought they could keep doing in Israel what they had always done, and it did not go well for them with Susanna: they were both put to death. Getting away with things makes you think you are good, but everything comes back to haunt you in this truth. We have to be men of honor.

A man who says he would sell his soul for a hundred million dollars has shown his character, and some sell it for a dollar: the crackhead sells his for a five dollar rock, the covetous man for a cheeseburger, a happy meal. If you are constantly sinning to acquire, you are selling your soul. Character makes a man predictable and dependable; once people know your character they know how to deal with you. If you need five dollars I could give you five dollars, but I will never do business with a covetous man.

“They have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.” Your name, your reputation, is everything in Israel. If you are messing up your name, it is because you are not reading. Once your name goes to mud it takes a lot of work to bring it back, and when it comes to money, nobody will deal with you.

“Thou shalt not steal.” If you tell me you are going to do a job for me, take my money and don't do it, did you steal? Did you lie? Were you covetous? Yes. One sin adds to another, and another, and another.

“Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is thy neighbour’s.” Covetousness will cause you to break every one of the ten commandments.

You become your own god, putting money or whatever you covet before God, and you go into idolatry. You break the Sabbath: you want money so bad you go to work, or you take a side job, or when the boss asks for extra hours you say the Lord understands. You bear false witness: you say you will do a job, take the money and never intend to do it. You kill: hating your neighbour and coveting his stuff is murder already, and literally, you steal and kill the witness so you don't go to jail, or you kill the dude who puts up a fight while you rob him. You commit adultery: you see your brother's wife, covet what is his when you have your own, and fall into it.

So if you are covetous, check your spirit, because you will break every law. A covetous man is his own god: he only sees himself, and whatever he wants is what is going to happen.

“Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth; fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence, and covetousness”. Covetousness is named specifically: you have to mortify that thing, because it is going to destroy you.

“And covetousness, which is idolatry”. Let it sink in. When you are covetous you are an idolater, because the only one you listen to is you. You are your own god and you worship you. Whatever you think is what it is, it makes sense in your head, and you don't seek counsel.

So a man must sit back and examine himself: you've done this and this and that, and everything you've done is along the lines of money. Where there's smoke, there's fire. Ten people cannot all have the same story about you while you say everybody is lying. That is denial. After the first person brought it out, you should have gone and made things right with the others; instead your heart was still set on hiding the rest. Did you take the money? Yes. Then your name is Mr. Covetous.

Many times we become covetous because we envy what other people have. Never hang your hat where you can't reach: live according to your means. A brother having money does not mean you covet everything he has; the man worked hard. Stay in your lane. We all work hard for our money, so if we entrust you with it, deliver and do what you said you would do.

“For which things’ sake the wrath of God cometh on the children of disobedience”. When you are covetous you are disobedient, and eventually the wrath of God comes upon you. You will watch the things that were supposed to be a blessing vanish away, and you may not understand it, but you should know exactly why: whatever happens to you happens because of your doings. There are things you say and do that bring death and curses to your door. If you want blessings, apply the laws, statutes and commandments. Walk in the spirit and you will never do amiss.

“No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.” Mammon is money: you cannot serve God and money.

This is why the elite don't want to hear anything about God: they feel they are in their heaven already. And this is why many are scared of dying. Many times the fear of death is not death itself, it is leaving their possessions behind.

precepts.why:
“O death, how bitter is the remembrance of thee to a man that liveth at rest in his possessions”. That man is living so good that the moment he thinks of death he says, I have to leave all this behind?

That is why in this truth you can't get attached to things. They loved not their lives unto the death; nothing on this planet can hold us back from doing what we are supposed to do. But a covetous man does not want to die after he just stole that nice Porsche and bought that nice house. He wants to enjoy it a little more, because to a covetous man it is never enough.

Because of his possessions his mind is on here, not on what the Most High has in store for us, which eyes have not seen nor ears heard. He wants it now: “unto the man that hath nothing to vex him, and that hath prosperity in all things: yea, unto him that is yet able to receive meat!”

sense.text:
“Many have sinned for a small matter”. They sinned because they are not walking in the spirit; that little situation should not have caused anyone to sin. A brother asks, can you do this job? That's nothing. Ten grand, done in two months. Two years later, no job and the money is gone. That is a small matter: you gave your word, and you must be a man of your word.

“And he that seeketh for abundance will turn his eyes away.” He wants it all, so he turns his eyes away from the truth and the laws of God. He knows what the Bible says, but the money is green, he's in love with Benjamin and Grant and Jackson and says the hell with Washington. He does it once, twice, three times, and before he knows it he's buried. Always put the Lord first.

Time shows your character. How you deal with a situation and how you bounce back from it is how we know what you are really about. Some fight in the truth the same spirit they had in the world, some find a spirit they never knew was there, and some always did shady business and hid it. But nothing can be hidden in here, because darkness and light can't dwell together: give it time and all your sins will be exposed. That is a good thing, because you want the Lord to show you your sins so you can repent and fix them. The word is sharper than any two-edged sword and cuts both ways: we all have something to pick up from this. Covet good gifts: covet a brother's skill and become his understudy, but don't hate him because he has it and you don't.

“As a nail sticketh fast between the joinings of the stones; so doth sin stick close between buying and selling.” It is very hard to pull a nail out of a stone, and sin sticks that close to buying and selling. The moment you talk business, sin says: I can help you make more money; they trust you; tell them the wood cost five thousand when you got it for three with your discount card, charge three for the job, and you come out with six. That is the devil playing tricks on you. That's a setup.

This is why business between brothers in the truth so often never ends well, and why you had better be well studied if you are going to do business. The moment you say you want to do business, you are entering a realm where demons are all around you, tempting you to see how righteous you will be.

“Unless a man hold himself diligently in the fear of the Lord, his house shall soon be overthrown.” Diligent: characterized by steady, earnest, and energetic effort; painstaking. You must be doing everything you can to hold yourself in the fear of the Lord. If you are not giving it all you've got, you're done.

Don't be here carelessly, just keeping the Sabbath. When you find yourself idle, doing nothing, you are chilling with the devil, because idleness teaches much evil. The number one way to hold yourself diligently is to read this Bible continuously and know its stories, because in them you learn the do's and don'ts. When you are in a situation, you remember Joseph: how did he get away? He ran.

So in business, if you don't hold yourself diligently you will do shady business, and shady business doesn't last. You thought you were going to be a big-time tycoon, and you end up garbage.

“But above all things, my brethren, swear not, neither by heaven, neither by the earth, neither by any other oath: but let your yea be yea; and your nay, nay; lest ye fall into condemnation.” When you say yes, I'm going to do it, do it. When you say no, you can't, then don't. But never say yes, get paid to do it, and then not do it.

Condemnation: the state of being condemned; to condemn is to declare to be reprehensible, wrong, or evil, usually after weighing evidence and without reservation. The Lord is going to judge you. He will review your case like a docket in court: how do you plead? Not guilty. Bring the witness. You didn't know they had witnesses, but the Lord knows everything. The eyes of the Lord are in every place, beholding the evil and the good, and a little bird carries the news.

You do evil in a different state with someone we never met, and another brother goes to that state for a job and meets that same person. What are the odds? When people are just minding their business and your evil comes up without anybody asking one question, that should make you reflect: the Most High is doing it that way because he wants you to get right. He could have let you do it to the wrong person, and we would find out when you were six feet under, shot in the back over a hundred grand. You can sit at home and hate me, or see that the Lord wants to help you. Recognize your mistakes, apologize, make amends, and walk in the spirit so that blessing may come your way.

precepts.why:
Matthew says it in a way you might get it, showing why you fall into condemnation: “But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.”

So you are evil when you lie to your brothers. Anything other than your yea being yea and your nay being nay is evil, and if you are evil you are going to be condemned, not by us but by the Lord, because his eyes are in every place beholding the evil and the good, and he rewards every man according to his deeds.

“Lie not one to another”. It is forbidden for us to lie one to another. We must be men of character, men of honor, because the world must look at us and say surely this is a wise and understanding people.

If you are lying, how is the world going to call you wise and understanding? They will say this is an evil ass negro, and now the truth is evil spoken of, because the whole time you were doing it you had fringes on your clothes. At no time did you look down at your fringes and say, I can't behave this way, I can't do this to my brother, not even to people in the world.

That is because you are not in the Bible. There is no way to be in the Bible and doing evil; the two don't go hand in hand. Nobody finishes reading thou shalt not steal and then goes and gets his gun. Give attendance to reading, continuously, so the word is in you.

sense.text:
“Moreover he must have a good report of them which are without”. Nobody in the world should have anything evil to say about you. Many in the world will lie on us, but nothing they say should they be able to back up. So if you do business in the world you must be twice as honorable, and if you are, you get more jobs, because nobody likes a thief and everybody wants to save a dollar. A developer will throw jobs at an honest man left and right. Penny wise, pound foolish: you make an extra penny on this job and lose the whole pound, and people stop calling you without saying why, because they saw what you tried to pull.

That is no way to live: ducking people, no longer going down a certain street, circling the block three times when you come home looking at every parked car, afraid somebody will hop out asking where's his money. Some dudes will pistol whip you or stab you up for twenty dollars, and it's about the principle.

“Lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil.” The devil traps you: he convinced you it was okay to lie, okay to steal, okay to be covetous, and at the end he removes himself, and the people you owe show up. After the beating you still have to give back the money, so why go through that? Deal righteously.

If you must have a good report with them that are without, how much better should your report be with them that are within? If you are doing good outside, you won't be doing bad here. The two go hand in hand.

“Let him that stole steal no more”. Stop stealing and get a job. You're not a businessman, you're a thief. Business is not for everybody; business is for people who have integrity. Get a job, and trust me, you'll do a lot better.

“But rather let him labour, working with his hands the thing which is good, that he may have to give to him that needeth.” One day you might have to give to somebody in the body who is in need, because the poor will always be with us. So don't be the one robbing the poor, the brother who saved his little two dollars for a job done. Be the one who works and has some bread, so that if a brother needs five you can give him five, and if he needs ten you can give him ten. Be the one giving, not the one taking.

precepts.why:
“Render therefore to all their dues: tribute to whom tribute is due; custom to whom custom; fear to whom fear; honour to whom honour.” Pay your debts. Pay your taxes. Don't go lying on your taxes to get an extra dollar: Esau sees everything, one day you'll get audited, and you'll have to pay everything back.

“Owe no man any thing”. No man should be able to say he owes me this much or that much because he took my money and never did the job. Had you been doing your four chapters a day and applying yourself, you would remember scriptures like this when the devil tempts you: it's cold outside and I don't feel like getting out of bed, but I took the man's money and said I would do the job, so let me get up and do it, because I don't want to owe anybody anything.

“But to love one another: for he that loveth another hath fulfilled the law.” You have to have love for your brother. Backdealing with your brother shows no love; that's hatred. By being covetous you break many laws, and you have a legion of demons on you that takes major prayer and fasting.

sense.text: “Thou shalt not have in thine house divers measures, a great and a small.” The Lord does not like people who are crooked. If you are going to do business, make sure you have a just balance. Don't tilt it.

“But thou shalt have a perfect and just weight, a perfect and just measure shalt thou have: that thy days may be lengthened in the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee.” Don't play with the scale and tilt it in your favor.

If you really read this verse and embodied it, would you be dealing unjustly in business? The Bible already tells you what will happen if you keep an unjust balance: your days will be shortened. One day somebody is going to realize you've been robbing them, and they're going to kill you. You'd be surprised what people will do for a dollar, and the Lord wrote about that from the very beginning.

The Most High is not a joke. He gives commandments telling you what to do to live: keep them so that you may have life. You want to deal right because you want to live long in the land the Most High gives you. This class is the Bible speaking life into all of us who are dealing with those spirits, and if you don't take heed, death is at the door waiting.

precepts.why: “A just weight and balance are the Lord’s: all the weights of the bag are his work.” If you deal with a just weight and balance you are in the spirit, and the Most High loves that thing.

“Divers weights, and divers measures, both of them are alike abomination to the Lord.” If you are not dealing right in your business, the Lord looks at you as an abomination, and eventually he puts your light out, because he already warned you.

If you want long life, have a just weight: that is the thing he is pleased in. With divers weights and divers measures the Lord is not pleased, and your days will be short. Dudes will kill you for a dollar.

“Stolen waters are sweet, and bread eaten in secret is pleasant.” You feel good when you make that extra money stealing.

“But he knoweth not that the dead are there; and that her guests are in the depths of hell.” That is condemnation. So don't be a thief. Deal righteously; deal according to the laws, statutes and commandments.

sense.text:
“Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.” When a man won't seek counsel, pride has kicked in, and if he were reading he would understand that pride goes before the fall.

Many times when a brother does a bad deal with a brother, both of them were out of the spirit, because the one who was defrauded never asked for counsel either: I want to do this job with so-and-so, what do you think? Once people have a little money in their pocket they feel grown: I own my own house, I bought it with my own money, I'm doing better than you, who are you for me to counsel with? Then months or years later, when everything falls apart, they want counsel. Your pride went before every enterprise, and destruction came with it.

precepts.why:
“Let reason go before every enterprize, and counsel before every action.” In everything you do, seek counsel, and if you seek counsel and apply it, things will go well for you.

But instead of seeking counsel, pride kicks in: I'm my own man, I do what I want. Counsel is needed before the enterprise, not after things fall apart. Blessed is he that readeth: if we apply what we read, we will be all right.

sense.text: “Now Naaman, captain of the host of the king of Syria, was a great man with his master, and honourable”, “a mighty man in valour, but he was a leper.” Remember Naaman the leper.
A little maid carried captive out of the land of Israel waited on Naaman’s wife and told her mistress there is a prophet in Israel who can heal him.

Anybody will give everything for their health; the Bible says that in Job. So Naaman took “ten talents of silver, and six thousand pieces of gold, and ten changes of raiment”, money, gold and letters: let's go see that man, I need to be cleansed.
Elisha said to the king of Israel, don't worry about it: “let him come now to me, and he shall know that there is a prophet in Israel.”
Elisha said go in the Jordan, dip yourself seven times, and that leprosy is going to be gone.

“But Naaman was wroth”: he thought the prophet would come out and “strike his hand over the place, and recover the leper.” Many times we want God to do things the way we want God to do them. Shush up and obey: it is going to be done the way the Bible says it is going to be done.

“Are not Abana and Pharpar, rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel?” His pride almost kept him from being healed, because he didn't want to do what the prophet said. Maybe the Jordan was murky and he said I'm not dipping in that water. That's pride. When the Lord says do, do; stop going against what the prophets of the Lord are saying.

“Then went he down, and dipped himself seven times in Jordan, according to the saying of the man of God: and his flesh came again like unto the flesh of a little child”. He finally did what the prophet said, and he was healed.

Naaman wanted to bless him because he had just been healed; a man will give everything he has for his health. But Elisha said “I will receive none.” Keep all your goods, you're healed, go about your business.
Naaman went his way, him and all his gold and all his treasure. Elisha would take nothing.

“But Gehazi, the servant of Elisha the man of God”: Elisha had a servant. “As the Lord liveth, I will run after him, and take somewhat of him.” He was covetous. Naaman came with big money and Gehazi was looking at all that glitter: you're really not going to take any of this? The man just wants to give it away.

“So Gehazi followed after Naaman.” The hell with that, I'm going to get me some gold. “My master hath sent me”: did his master send him? No. Covetousness will make you lie. He coveted that silver and those garments, so he lied. But remember, God sees it all.

Elisha asks “Whence comest thou, Gehazi?” and he says “Thy servant went no whither.” He lies again. He is adding sin unto sin because he didn't control his covetousness, and now he has to lie and lie again.

“Went not mine heart with thee, when the man turned again from his chariot to meet thee?” How did he know? A little bird: the spirit of the Lord reveals. You think you're safe. Like the brother the bishop asked twice whether he was dealing drugs, who said no both times, and the next class the bishop played a video of him on the run after they raided his weed house. When the Lord sends the prophets to ask you about something you told nobody, take heed: I am doing it, and I'm good at hiding it, how would he know?

“The leprosy therefore of Naaman shall cleave unto thee, and unto thy seed for ever. And he went out from his presence a leper as white as snow.” The same sickness that had just left Naaman jumped on him, because of his covetousness. God does not like covetous people, and Gehazi was judged immediately.

Many of us think we are good because we aren't judged right away. But when the Lord is giving warnings and classes like this are coming out, some won't listen and will continue in their ways, and the same money they love so much will destroy them. Gehazi got destroyed.
“Now therefore hearken unto me, O ye children: for blessed are they that keep my ways.” You want to be blessed? Read the Bible, understand it, and keep what it says to do.
“Hear instruction, and be wise, and refuse it not.” If you refuse the instruction of God, you are choosing death.

“Blessed is the man that heareth me, watching daily at my gates, waiting at the posts of my doors.” How do you hear God's words? The Bible. Where is the gate of the Lord? The Bible. So meditate on it day and night, and you won't do amiss: money won't take your mind, you'll fight the lust within you, and you'll know how to deal with your brothers and sisters righteously. Do these things and you have nothing to worry about, because the word will be in you, and whenever life gets at you, you will be able to do the right thing.
“For whoso findeth me findeth life, and shall obtain favour of the Lord.” You get favor from the Lord if you watch daily at his gates and keep his sayings.

“But he that sinneth against me wrongeth his own soul”: you read it, you know what it says, and you choose to do the opposite. It's going to be bad for you. We have dealt mainly with stealing and covetousness, but sin is sin, so we all need to take inventory and ask whether in all our ways we are going against the Lord, and the only way to know is to read the Bible.

“All they that hate me love death.” You show you hate God when he says do A and you choose B, like a sister told to obey her lord who says I am the lord, I don't obey nobody. In every part of your life, measure yourself against the scriptures: can I back up what I just said or did with the law that says do it, or with the law that says don't?

Life is going to get at you; this is not a walk in the park. “Therefore let us lie in wait for the righteous”: you say you're righteous, so the wicked say, all right, I'm going to lay some traps for you. “He is clean contrary to our doings”: the way we live is contrary to the world. “He upbraideth us with our offending the law”: we teach and speak against the system and what is going on out here.
“He professeth to have the knowledge of God: and he calleth himself the child of the Lord.” We all say we have the knowledge of God, and we call ourselves the children of the Lord.
“He was made to reprove our thoughts.” The wicked know what the righteous were created for.
“He is grievous unto us even to behold”: they hate the sight of you. “His ways are of another fashion”: we have fringes and beards, we keep the laws.

“We are esteemed of him as counterfeits”: we say they are fake Jews and fake Christians. “He abstaineth from our ways as from filthiness”: we don't do Halloween, the Fourth of July, Christmas or Valentine's Day; those are filth. “Maketh his boast that God is his father”: we boast that we are the sons of the living God, that we are blessed, that we will inherit the kingdom and have Esau in chains.

“Let us see if his words be true: and let us prove what shall happen in the end of him.” You talk a good one, but are you doing what you're supposed to be doing? Because you talk that good one, you are going to be tested and put in situations where you have to back up your words. If it's just a show, the best Sabbath face on while you do bad dealings, run your mouth against your lord and want nothing to do with these laws, how will you survive when your trial comes? Take heed.

“Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent”. Don't play with it, don't caress it, don't charm it. When you see sin, flee from it.

“For if thou comest too near it, it will bite thee”. Some of you play with sin so much that you're within striking distance. Because the snake is coiled up you think you're safe at a foot away, but its striking distance could be two feet, and by the time you take two steps you're done. Joseph put his Nikes on and was out: he had never been with a woman, and when she took hold of him he knew if he didn't run, he was done. Many of us like to entertain sin a little more, and end up in the deep miry clay, in a dunghill.

“The teeth thereof are as the teeth of a lion, slaying the souls of men.” The devil is out there like a raging lion, roaming about seeking whom he may devour, smelling everybody, coming back tomorrow, and then heads off. Why? Because you entertained your sins. Keep yourself in the laws.

“He made man, and put his heart in the midst of the body, and gave him breath, life, and understanding.” God is the one who created us. Off of that alone you should know you can't hide anything from him: he gave you the mind, the heart, the lungs, everything you have. Why would you try to hide things from the Lord? You think you're going to get away with it?

He “searcheth out all hidden things in the secrets of the earth”. He knows every secret and hidden thing of this earth. Read your Bible: that might put the fear of the Lord in you and stop you sinning.

“Surely he knoweth your inventions”: not maybe, surely. He knows everything you're doing and the evil thoughts you had. “And what ye think in your hearts”: men may not know what's in your heart, but the Lord knows. “Even them that sin, and would hide their sin”: you sin and hide it and think nobody knows, but the Lord knows. Fear God, not men. What can men do, put you out of the body? The Lord can put you out of this earth. Fear that, and if you are keeping the law, nobody's going to judge you.
“He will put you all to shame.” The Lord will always put you to shame if you keep your sins up. You aren't getting away with anything.

“And when your sins are brought forth, ye shall be ashamed before men”. There are two kinds of shame: the shame of this world, and the righteous shame that brings you to repentance. If your shame is the shame of this world, you're dead already; you need the shame that brings you to repentance.

“And your own sins shall be your accusers in that day.” So you can't hate me or anybody else because your sins came out. Your own sins accuse you: did you do it? Yes. If anything, be glad your sins were found out, because with this scripture from the Lord we are trying to help you get your mind right. Don't get sad, get glad.

“Behold, God himself is the judge, fear him”. Not me, not anybody: God himself is the judge. He uses us as a mouthpiece, but the words are straight from the Lord. “Leave off from your sins, and forget your iniquities, to meddle no more with them for ever”: leave them alone, stop the evil you're doing, take inventory, develop a conscience and say I'm tired of being that person, I want to live according to the Lord's statutes and commandments.

“So shall God lead you forth, and deliver you from all trouble.” That is the only way God will lead you forth and deliver you. With secret sins you're always getting sick, something is always wrong with you, and as much as you steal you never have money.
“Seek ye the Lord while he may be found”. Right now the Lord can be found because the Lord is looking for you; otherwise classes like this wouldn't come out. “Call ye upon him while he is near”.

“Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts”: the trials of men are their own reasoning. You have your way of thinking and the Lord has his, so pick the Lord's way and let go of your own wicked ways. “And let him return unto the Lord, and he will have mercy upon him; and to our God, for he will abundantly pardon.”

“For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the Lord. For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways”. So which way should we pick? The Lord's ways. And if you don't, you are going to die.
